clue.text: Pinch to put pressure on

blocks.note: first meaning: to nip something tightly between fingers
second meaning: to lean on someone, as in forcing a concession

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction, pinch in order to apply pressure, but the two phrases are separate meanings of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both nipping between finger and thumb and coercing someone into giving way, as with a financial clampdown.

clue.text: Two pints each round initially in this part of town

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: a quart is two pints
the opening letters of each and round

explanation.surface: Ordering two pints all round at a pub in this neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A city quarter is a district, such as the Latin Quarter, a distinct area within a town.

clue.text: Prince seen on English lake, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word for lake counts by its sound

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a mere is a lake, common in English place names

explanation.surface: A royal spotted boating on a lake in England.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the lake beneath the English letter. The answer is a variant spelling of emir, a Muslim ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a ruler or nobleman in Muslim countries, a title commonly glossed as a prince.

clue.text: To Zulu, a louse may be full of enthusiasm

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could take another form, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: Zulu is the NATO alphabet word for Z
taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: To a Zulu, a parasite might be an object of keen interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealous person is fervent and eager, the adjective for someone keenly devoted to a cause.

clue.text: Collected one hundred said to be unrefined

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so the sound of the next word counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: a, as in 'a single one'
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
crude means unrefined, as with crude oil

explanation.surface: A tally of a hundred items gathered, described as rough and unpolished.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, the last syllables of the answer sound just like 'crude'; the letters are spelt to fit the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest or debts that have accrued have built up or been gathered over time, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: More shrewd accountant at first gives in each report

indicators.note: at first means at the start, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: CA is a chartered accountant
the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A sharper accountant initially concedes in every financial statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks as if it belongs to the accountant, but it applies to the four words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cagey means wary and guarded, unwilling to commit, so the comparative describes someone more cautious and canny.

clue.text: Moved established location again

blocks.note: first meaning: relocated people to a new home
second meaning: set up home somewhere once more

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about relocating, but the opening word and the rest are two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Refugees resettled elsewhere have been relocated and have put down roots in a new place a second time.

clue.text: Leave out former spouse — that's badly clued!

indicators.note: badly means done wrong, so the letters of the word beside it are put out of order

blocks.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A self-mocking crossword complaint: ignoring an ex is a poor clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter jokes that the clue is badly written; the remark is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude is to omit or keep out, a direct synonym for leaving something out.

clue.text: Overtaking, need the Queen make the grade?

definitions.note: infinitive phrase for a present participle: 'making the grade' would match exactly

blocks.note: passing another car is overtaking it
a must is a need, something required
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A learner asks whether overtaking is needed to pass a driving test with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition by example. ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass muster is the idiom for being found acceptable on inspection, as soldiers were on parade.

clue.text: Master sped away from amazing stampede

indicators.note: amazing suggests something astonishingly mixed up, so the letters of the following word are scrambled
going away from a word means leaving it, so the named letters are removed from it

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to remove
taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A rider bolted clear of an astonishing cattle rush.
explanation.walkthrough: Once the four letters of 'sped' leave 'stampede', what remains already reads in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a wild animal or a skill is to tame it, bringing it under control as a verb.

clue.text: Pain relief when casing seal is broken

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Medicine leaking out once the packaging's seal cracks.
explanation.definitionFit: These are painkilling drugs such as aspirin or paracetamol, the plural noun for remedies that relieve pain.

clue.text: Reset about zero, which produces all-round sound

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or moved here and there, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
O looks like a zero

explanation.surface: Turning a dial back to zero to get surround-sound audio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reset' looks like an instruction, but it is simply part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereo audio uses two channels from separate speakers, giving listeners a sense of sound coming from around them.

clue.text: Range for cooking crumpets

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters of the next word are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A kitchen stove ready for toasting crumpets at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' wants to be the cooker, matching 'cooking'; it means a span instead. A crumpet is a British griddle cake, eaten toasted.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full spread of values or options between extremes, such as a broad span of opinion.

clue.text: Concert's first person to perform has prospects

definitions.note: verb phrase for an adjective: 'is promising' would match exactly

blocks.note: a Prom is a promenade concert, as in the London BBC Proms
I is the first-person pronoun
to sing is to perform a song

explanation.surface: The opening act at a concert is a rising talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' looks like the opening performer, but it is the grammar term for the pronoun I. The Proms are a famous London summer series of concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shows promise is likely to succeed later, so they have good future chances.

clue.text: Bootlegged product is trash!

blocks.note: first meaning: illegally distilled liquor
second meaning: foolish talk, nonsense

explanation.surface: A grumble that smuggled liquor is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both illicitly made spirits, brewed by night, and fanciful nonsense not worth believing.

clue.text: Transform part of central terrace

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Renovating a section of a row of houses in the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change it, a plain synonym for making it different in form.

clue.text: Unruly chav gains nothing, causing disruption

indicators.note: unruly means out of order and badly behaved, so the letters of the next word are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written; a chav is British slang for a loutish youth
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A rowdy youth who got away with nothing still caused trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gains' adds the letter for nothing to the fodder before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread chaos and damage, so causing it means creating serious disorder.

clue.text: A little baby, small and woeful

indicators.note: a little means only a small portion is taken, a stretch of letters inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the comma between the two words

explanation.surface: A tiny, sickly infant looking miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' looks like part of the description of the baby; it is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means dreadfully bad, the adjective for something appallingly poor in quality.

clue.text: Little devil’s downfall is in the offing

blocks.note: an imp is a small devil or mischievous sprite
a downfall is a finish or ruin

explanation.surface: A mischievous sprite's ruin is coming soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the offing is about to happen, the idiom for an event that is looming or imminent.

clue.text: Correspondence about politeness son left out

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around, so what remains is rearranged
left out means omitted, so the named letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, letters to remove

explanation.surface: A letter complaining about the courtesy a son forgot.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters of son come out of the fodder from separate places before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, like those of the apostles, so it is a piece of correspondence.

clue.text: Unworldliness shown in vain trip by Egypt's young

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters of the word before it fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder
ET is the international vehicle code for Egypt
Y is an abbreviation for young

explanation.surface: Innocence displayed by youngsters on a pointless Egyptian holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' wants to be a journey to Egypt; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence and inexperience, lacking the worldly wisdom that comes with age.

clue.text: Oil for great comfort

blocks.note: Gr is an abbreviation for great, as in Gr Britain
ease is comfort, freedom from hardship

explanation.surface: Lubricant offering great relief.
explanation.definitionFit: To grease a hinge is to lubricate it, and as a noun it is a thick lubricating substance like oil.

clue.text: Sties are blots on the landscape

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: styes are sore places on the eye
second meaning: ugly buildings that spoil a view

explanation.surface: Pigsties spoil the look of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sties' looks like pig pens, but here it is the eye infection, so the answer splits as EYE SORES.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsightly building or structure is called this idiomatically, something that offends anyone who sees it.

clue.text: Press ninety-nine when dry

blocks.note: to press clothes is to iron them
IC is ninety-nine in Roman numerals, one less than a hundred

explanation.surface: Ironing laundry at ninety-nine degrees once it has dried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like the state of the laundry, but it means a deadpan kind of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry wit says the opposite of what it means with a straight face, which is the hallmark of irony.

clue.text: Happen to see officer in command around the old city

blocks.note: OC stands for officer commanding
c is circa, Latin for around, used with dates
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Chancing to meet the commanding officer near an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal, but here it supplies a letter: the abbreviation for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to take place or come about, a plain synonym for an event happening.

clue.text: In two minds about evil batman

indicators.note: about suggests turning things around, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Undecided whether to root for a darker, wicked version of the caped superhero.
explanation.walkthrough: A batman is also an army officer's servant, but here only the letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being undecided between conflicting feelings is the idiom, so holding mixed attitudes toward something matches.

clue.text: Lines for an American spoken as signals for action on stage

indicators.note: spoken means said out loud, so the word is chosen for its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: what an American calls lines, Britons call queues

explanation.surface: An actor's lines for a US production, delivered as prompts on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' wants to be the script, fitting the stage scene; it is people waiting in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre cues are the words or actions telling a performer when to enter or speak.

clue.text: Again peels back to reveal a spy

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so the built word is read from its end

blocks.note: the prefix re- means again
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone peels back a covering a second time to expose a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peels back' reads as one phrase, but 'back' is the turnaround signal for the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is an agent planted long in advance who lies dormant until activated by their handlers.

clue.text: Flutters around beam of light in shops

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word goes on either side of the other

blocks.note: a flutter is British slang for a small bet
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Gambling stakes and sunbeams in retail stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shops' looks like stores but is the British slang verb: to shop someone is to inform on them. A flutter is a small wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Informing on someone to the police is betrayal, so the third-person verb matches the slang sense.
